newsitem.title: UK: Mexico HFS set to expand, challenge sugar -Licht.
newsitem.headline: Mexico HFS set to expand, challenge sugar -Licht.

text.p: Mexico's production of high fructose syrup (HFS) is likely to expand and then challenge the role of sugar in the country's sweeteners market, German analyst F.O. Licht said on Thursday.
Production could soon take off in the HFS sector, with two new plants having already started production.
Licht, in the latest edition of its International Sugar and Sweetener Report, estimated Mexican HFS output would surge to 120,000 tonnes in 1996/97 from just 25,000 the previous year.
Licht cited industry sources as saying overall HFS output would reach 350,000 to 400,000 tonnes in the next few years.
Rising HFS consumption could soon put Mexico high up on the list of worldwide consumers.
"There are good chances that HFS consumption will grow rapidly in the years to come," Licht said.

It estimated Mexican HFS offtake to reach somewhat less than 300,000 tonnes in 1996/97, putting the country in fourth position in the international consumer league after the U.S., Japan and the European Union.

"While there will continue to be imports from the U.S., particularly covering the requirements in the border region...these tonnages are likely to stagnate as additional demand will be absorbed by domestic production," the report said.
